quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #24
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When you plan to pass another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Do not assume the other driver will make room for you to return to your lane.
Assume the other driver will let you pass if you use your turn signal.
Assume the other driver will stay at the same speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not assume the other driver will make room for you to return to your lane.
questions.explanation: Even if you signal, do not assume that other drivers will give you space or the right of way.

questions.question: What color are regulatory signs?

options.text: Green.
Yellow.
White.

questions.correctAnswerText: White.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers about traffic laws they must follow. These signs are usually white squares or rectangles with black, red, or green letters or symbols.

questions.question: When is highway pavement most slippery?

options.text: After it has been raining for several hours.
When rain just begins.
After it has been raining for one to two hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: When rain just begins.
questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery when it first starts to rain. Dirt and oil on the road mix with rainwater and create a slick surface.

questions.question: When should you return to your original lane after passing a vehicle?

options.text: When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
When you have cleared the front bumper of the passed vehicle.
When you are 50 feet in front of the passed vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Move back into your lane only when you can see the other vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror. This means you have enough space to safely get back in front of them.

questions.question: A driver license is a:

options.text: Requirement.
Privilege.
Right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Privilege.
questions.explanation: Driving is a privilege, not a right. All drivers must help keep roads safe. If you misuse this privilege, it can be taken away.

questions.question: If the rear of your vehicle skids to the left, what should you do?

options.text: Do not turn your steering wheel.
Turn your steering wheel to the left.
Turn your steering wheel to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel to the left.
questions.explanation: If you skid on a wet or icy road, take your foot off the gas, do not use the brakes, and turn your steering wheel in the direction of the skid. If you have anti-lock brakes, apply them firmly and steer straight.

questions.question: What must you do on a green arrow?

options.text: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.
Yield to pedestrians only.
Wait four seconds before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can go. Turn in the direction the arrow points after you yield to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians still in the intersection.

questions.question: What can you do on a roadway with a broken white centerline?

options.text: You must stay in your lane.
You may cross the centerline to change lanes.
You may change lanes only from the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may cross the centerline to change lanes.
questions.explanation: White lines between lanes mean both lanes go in the same direction. A broken white line means you can pass another vehicle when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: If your car begins to skid out of control, what should you do?

options.text: Pump the brakes.
Apply light brake pressure.
Avoid using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid using the brakes.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, do not brake. Keep steering until your vehicle is under control and moving safely.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Yield to all traffic before crossing.
Stop, then enter when it is safe.
Slow down and cross carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and cross carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down to a safe speed and proceed with caution.

questions.question: When parking your vehicle on a hill, what should you do?

options.text: Touch one rear wheel to the curb.
Use your parking brake and put the vehicle in "park."
Point your front wheels parallel to the road if there is no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your parking brake and put the vehicle in "park."
questions.explanation: Always use your parking brake and put the vehicle in "park" when parking on a hill. If there is no curb, turn your front wheels away from the road center so the car rolls away if brakes fail. If there is a curb, turn wheels toward it when going downhill, or away from it when going uphill.

questions.question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, where should you turn?

options.text: Into any lane.
Into the first lane.
Into the second lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Into the first lane.
questions.explanation: Always turn from your lane into the first available legal lane. When turning from a two-way street to a one-way street, turn into the first lane.

questions.question: What do broken yellow lines mean on streets and highways?

options.text: No passing is allowed.
They separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.
They separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: They separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Broken lines mean you may pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When entering a freeway, how should you check traffic?

options.text: Use your rearview and side mirrors.
Use your rearview mirror only.
Use your side mirror and look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your side mirror and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: When entering a freeway, use your side mirror and look over your shoulder to see traffic clearly and avoid blind spots.

questions.question: What does an orange and red triangular sign on a vehicle mean?

options.text: The vehicle has the right-of-way.
It is a slow-moving vehicle.
There is construction work ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is a slow-moving vehicle.
questions.explanation: Orange and red triangles are used on slow-moving vehicles like farm tractors, road maintenance vehicles, and horse-drawn carts.

questions.question: If you miss your freeway exit, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Continue on the freeway and find another route.
Go to the next exit, leave the freeway, and return to the correct exit.
Back up on the road or shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Back up on the road or shoulder.
questions.explanation: Never back up on a freeway road or shoulder. Continue to the next exit. Backing up causes accidents because other drivers will not expect it.

questions.question: What does this sign warn you about?

options.text: A construction flagger is ahead.
A police officer is ahead.
A parking attendant is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A construction flagger is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a flagger ahead. Always follow the flagger's directions. Flaggers wear orange or yellow vests and use paddles and flags to direct traffic through work zones.

questions.question: When your view at an intersection is blocked, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down and look both ways.
Keep your speed and look both ways.
Stop, then slowly move forward until you can see clearly both ways.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then slowly move forward until you can see clearly both ways.
questions.explanation: Stop completely at the intersection. Then inch forward slowly until you can see clearly in both directions before proceeding.

questions.question: In bad weather, what should you do?

options.text: Drive off the road.
Drive in a low gear.
Steer and brake smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer and brake smoothly.
questions.explanation: In bad weather, avoid sudden braking and sharp turns. Smooth steering and gentle braking help you control your vehicle better.

questions.question: How long do passenger restrictions apply to new license holders?

options.text: Three months
12 months
Six months

questions.correctAnswerText: 12 months
questions.explanation: New drivers have passenger restrictions for 12 months. For the first 6 months, only instructors, parents, or guardians can ride with them. For the next 6 months, only immediate family members can ride with them.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should never:

options.text: Change lanes while inside an intersection.
Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.
Check for other drivers entering the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes while inside an intersection.
questions.explanation: Never change lanes inside an intersection. Always look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Watch for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.question: You cannot park within how many feet of a fire hydrant?

options.text: 20 feet
15 feet
10 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 10 feet
questions.explanation: Do not park within 10 feet of a fire hydrant at any time.

questions.question: Your vehicle wheels have run off the pavement. What should you do first?

options.text: Turn the steering wheel slightly left to get back on the pavement.
Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas pedal, and gently apply the brakes.
Apply the brakes and turn the steering wheel sharply to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas pedal, and gently apply the brakes.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas pedal, and gently apply the brakes. Slow down and check traffic before safely returning to the road. Do not jerk the steering wheel sharply, as this can cause you to lose control or enter another lane.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, move back to the right lane when:

options.text: You are one car length ahead of the other vehicle.
You can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.
You are 50 feet ahead of the other vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Only pass when you have enough space to return to the driving lane safely. Make sure there is enough room between you and the vehicle you passed. When you see both headlights in your rearview mirror, it is safe to move back to the right lane.

questions.question: You must yield to an emergency vehicle with its siren and flashing lights by:

options.text: Moving to the right edge of the road and stopping.
Moving to the right lane and driving slowly until it passes.
Stopping immediately, even if you are in an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Moving to the right edge of the road and stopping.
questions.explanation: Yield the right-of-way to any emergency vehicle using its siren and flashing lights. Move to the right edge of the road and stop. Do not stop in an intersection. You can move again after the emergency vehicle passes.
